neighbours.label: Existential 'there is (no) X' statements about whether something exists or is defined (no value defined, no such thing as, no matching record), firing on the slot after the existential noun, vs plain descriptive sentences without an existence claim
fire: The parser raises an error if there is no closing bracket in the expression.
In this village there is no doctor, so patients travel to the next town.
When there is a duplicate key in the file, the loader keeps the last value.
Philosophers have argued that there is no such thing as a purely selfless act.

# there is no entry for this id yet, so create one
    cache[id] = build(id)
The report found there is no evidence of fraud in the company accounts.
If there is an existing session for the user, the server reuses it.
Some claim there is no single correct way to brew a cup of coffee.
quiet: The parser reads the expression from left to right and builds a tree.
In this village the doctor visits on Tuesdays and treats patients at home.
The loader reads each line of the file and stores the value in a dictionary.
Philosophers have argued about selflessness since the time of the ancient Greeks.

# build the entry for this id and store it
    cache[id] = build(id)
The report praised the company accounts for their clarity and detail.
The server stores each session in memory for thirty minutes.
Some people brew coffee in a French press every morning before work.

predictions: Sentences stating whether something exists reach 0.2-0.45 at or after the existential noun; descriptive sentences of the same topic without 'there is/no X' stay under 0.15. Negation itself does not matter.
notes: Card: peaks after 'no value defined', 'a location without a name', 'No existing person', 'no such thing as', 'no before and after'. Probe: no value set 0.335, a value set 0.331 (affirmative also fires), no matching record 0.353, a matching entry 0.424, no such thing 0.359; museum hours 0.021; 'if not user' 0.169, 'if user' 0.076.
